Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:10:1.hebrew: תורת הזמה לא פריך - אינה חשובה לו פירכא, דכיון דעד אחד ישנו בהזמה ליבטל עדותו בעדות שני עדים, אם הוה לן למימר בעדים משום דישנן בהזמה לא יחייבוהו שבועה, הוה לן למימר נמי בעד אחד לא יחייבהו שבועה, דהא ישנו בהזמה ליבטל עדותו. ואי משום דאין משלם קנס, אין בזו יפוי כח להאמין עדותו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:10:1.english: [He] does not refute [based on] the law of conspiring witnesses - This is not considered a [valid] refutation to him. For since a single witness is subject to [the law of] conspiring witnesses, to have his testimony nullified through the testimony of two witnesses, if we were to say regarding [two] witnesses that because they are subject to [the law of] conspiring witnesses, they should not obligate him [to take] an oath, we would also have to say regarding a single witness that he should not obligate him [to take] an oath, for he too is subject to [the law of] conspiring witnesses, to have his testimony nullified. And if [the distinction is] because [a single witness] does not pay a fine, this does not provide any added strength to believe his testimony.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:1.hebrew: אלא דקאמר ותנא תונא - אלא, אם יש לך להשיב על דברי רבי חייא, כך יש לך להשיב: דקאמר ותנא תונא, והביא ראיה לדבריו ממשנתינו, מי דמי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:1.english: Rather, that which he said: "And the tanna taught [similarly]" - Rather, if you have [an objection] to raise against the words of Rabbi Ḥiyya, this is what you have to reply: That he said, "And the tanna taught [similarly]," and brought proof for his words from our mishna — is it comparable?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:2.english: There - In [the case] of Rabbi Ḥiyya.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:3.english: The creditor has witnesses - That he is owed fifty by him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:4.english: The debtor does not have witnesses - Regarding the other fifty, that he does not owe him for them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:5.hebrew: אי הוה ליה כו' - כגון אילו העידו העדים: חמשים חייב, וחמשים פרע — בכה"ג לא הוה אמר ר' חייא דצריך לישבע על השאר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:5.english: If [the debtor] had, etc. - For example, if the witnesses had testified: "He owes fifty, and fifty he repaid" — in such a case, Rabbi Ḥiyya would not have said that he is required to take an oath regarding the remainder.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:6.english: Just as we are witnesses for this one - That half of it is his.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:7.hebrew: אנן סהדי להאי - דחציה שלו. ולמה הצריכוהו חכמים שבועה? ש"מ, טעמא לאו משום מודה מקצת הטענה הוא כר' חייא, ואינה שבועה דאורייתא, אלא תקנת חכמים, שלא יהא כל אחד הולך כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:11:7.english: We are witnesses for this one - That half of it is his. And why did the Sages require him to take an oath? Conclude from this that the reason is not on account of an admission to part of the claim according to Rabbi Ḥiyya, and it is not a Torah-mandated oath, but rather an enactment of the Sages, so that not everyone will go, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:12:1.hebrew: והילך - לא הוצאתים, והן שלך בכ"מ שהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:12:1.english: And here you are - I have not spent them, and they are yours wherever they are.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:12:2.hebrew: חייב - לישבע על השאר, ולא אמרינן: הני דקמודי ליה בגוייהו, הואיל ואיתנהו בעינייהו, כמאן דנקיט להו דמי; אלא כשאר מודה במקצת הוא, וחייב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:12:2.english: [He is] obligated - To take an oath regarding the remainder, and we do not say: These [coins] that he admits to [owing] him, since they are intact, are considered as though [the creditor] is [already] holding them; rather, he is like any other [person who] admits to part of a claim, and is obligated [to take an oath].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:14:1.hebrew: ותנא תונא כו' - קס"ד דלר' חייא טעמא דמתני' משום דאנן סהדי דמאי דתפיס דיליה הוא, והוי כמנה לי בידך, והלה אמר אין לך בידי כלום, והעדים מעידים אותו שיש לו חמשים, וכי אידך דרבי חייא, דמחייב ליה שבועה דאורייתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:14:1.english: And the Tanna taught [similarly], etc. - The Gemara initially thought that according to Rabbi Ḥiyya, the reason for the mishna is because we are witnesses that what he holds is his, and [thus] it is like: "I have a maneh in your possession, and the other said: You have nothing of mine in my possession, and the witnesses testify about him that he has fifty," and like the other [ruling] of Rabbi Ḥiyya, which obligates him in a Torah oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:15:1.hebrew: והא הכא - דהך העדאת עדים, אנן סהדי דמאי דתפיס האי הילך הוא, שהרי בפנינו הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:15:1.english: And is it not [the case] here - For in this testimony of witnesses, we are witnesses that what this [party] is holding is "here you are," for it is before us.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:15:2.hebrew: וקתני - דמחייב שבועה אשארא, וה"ה להודאה במקצת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:15:2.english: And [the mishna] teaches - That he is obligated [to take] an oath on the remainder, and the same applies to an admission to part [of a claim].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:17:1.hebrew: תקנת חכמים היא - ולא משום העדאת עדים, וכדפרכינן לעיל: כי היכי דאנן סהדי להאי, אנן סהדי להאי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:17:1.english: It is a rabbinic ordinance - And not due to the testimony of witnesses, as we objected above: "Just as we are witnesses for this one, [so too] we are witnesses for that one."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:18:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא מדאורייתא חייב - כלומר, גבי שבועה דאורייתא, כגון בהודאה במקצת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:18:1.english: Granted, if you say that by Torah law [he is] obligated - That is to say, with regard to a Torah oath, such as in [the case of] admission to part [of a claim].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:1:1.hebrew: תאמר - בשבועה דעדים, שאינו נשבע על מה שהעידו, אלא על מה שלא העידו, ועל כפירתו הוא נשבע ולא אהעדאתן, ומנין לך להחמיר כל כך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:1:1.english: Would you say - [Would you say this] with regard to an oath [imposed by] witnesses, where he does not swear about what they testified, but rather about what they did not testify, and it is upon his denial that he swears, and not upon their testimony? And from where do you [derive a basis] to be so stringent?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:2:1.hebrew: מגלגול שבועה דעד אחד - אם נתחייב לו שבועה ע"י עד אחד, כדאמרינן, והיתה עליו טענה אחרת שלא היתה מוטלת עליו שבועה, מגלגלין אותה עם שבועה זאת, ונשבע על שניהן, דגלגול שבועה דאורייתא היא, דילפינן לה בקדושין (דף כז:) מואמרה האשה אמן אמן. הרי שעל מה שלא העיד העד הוא משביעו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:2:1.english: From the extension of an oath of a single witness - If he became obligated to him [to take] an oath by means of a single witness, as we said, and there was another claim against him for which an oath was not incumbent upon him, we extend it along with this oath, and he takes an oath regarding both of them; for the extension of an oath is from the Torah, as we derive it in Kiddushin (27b) from: "And the woman shall say: Amen, Amen." Behold, [we see] that he makes him take an oath regarding that which the witness did not testify.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:3:1.hebrew: שכן שבועה גוררת שבועה - עד לא חייבו שבועה אלא על מה שהעיד, והשבועה גוררת שבועה. תאמר בעדים הללו, שהחמשים שהעידוהו הם מחייבין אותו לשלם, ואין כאן שבועה לגרור על ידה שבועה על השאר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:3:1.english: For an oath draws [another] oath - A [single] witness only obligated him [to take] an oath on what he testified to, and the oath draws [another] oath [in its wake]. Would you say [the same] regarding these witnesses, where they obligate him to pay the fifty [zuz] about which they testified against him, and there is no oath here through which to draw an oath on the remainder?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:4:1.hebrew: פיו יוכיח - מודה מקצת הטענה, שעל מה שכופר ופיו לא הודה הוא נשבע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:4:1.english: His mouth can prove [it] - [This refers to] one who admits to part of the claim, for regarding that which he denies and his mouth did not admit, he takes an oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:6:1.hebrew: טענה וכפירה - זה טוען וזה כופר, הן באין לדין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:6:1.english: A claim and a denial - This one claims and that one denies, [and thus] they come to court.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:7:1.hebrew: לא הוחזק כפרן - על מה שכפר אינו מוחזק כפרן, שמא לא כיחש, שהעד אינו נאמן להכחישו ולהחזיקו כפרן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:7:1.english: He has not been established as a denier - Regarding what he denied, he is not established as a denier, for perhaps he did not falsely deny [it], as the [single] witness is not believed to contradict him and establish him as a denier.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:7:2.hebrew: תאמר בעדים - שמאחר שכפר הכל, והם העידו על החמשים, הוחזק כפרן, ולא נאמר נאמינהו על השבועה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:7:2.english: Would you say [the same] regarding witnesses - For since he denied everything and they testified about the fifty, he has been established as a denier, and we do not say: "Let us believe him regarding the oath."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:8:1.hebrew: הכופר במלוה - בין על כולה, בין על מקצת, ובאו עדים והעידוהו עד שלא נשבע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:8:1.english: One who denies a loan - Whether [he denied] all of it or part of it, and witnesses came and testified against him before he took an oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:8:2.hebrew: כשר לעדות - ולא אמרינן גזלן הוא, והתורה אמרה (שמות כג) אל תשת רשע עד — דכיון דמלוה להוצאה נתנה, דלמא צריך להוציאה, וסבר: עד דהוה לי [זוזי] ופרענא ליה, ואי מודינא ליה השתא, יתבעני מיד. אבל הכופר בפקדון, אפילו על מקצת, ובאו עדים והעידוהו — פסול לעדות, דמאי הוה ליה גבי פקדון לאשתמוטי נפשיה? ושמא תאמר: אבד ממנו, ואשתמיט ליה עד דמשכח ליה — לקמן בפירקין (בבא מציעא דף ה:) מוקמינן בדאתו סהדי ואמרי: ההיא שעתא בידיה נקיט ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:8:2.english: Is fit to bear witness - And we do not say [that] he is a robber, and [yet] the Torah said (Exodus 23:1): "Do not place a wicked person as a witness"—for since a loan is given to be spent, perhaps he needed to spend it, and he thought: "[I will stall] until I have [money] and I will repay him; for if I admit to him now, he will demand payment from me immediately." However, one who denies [having received] a deposit, even [denying only] part [of it], and witnesses came and testified against him, is disqualified from bearing witness, for what [reason] would he have regarding a deposit to evade [the claim]? And lest you say: It was lost from him, and he evaded him until he could find it—later in our chapter (Bava Metzia 5b), we establish [it as a case] where witnesses came and said: "At that very moment, he was holding it in his hand."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:9:1.hebrew: בתורת הזמה - לשלם קנס דכאשר זמם, דעד אחד שהוזם פטור, ופיו גבי הודאה, כל שכן דלא שייכא הזמה כלל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:9:1.english: [Subject] to the law of hazamah - [That is,] to pay the penalty of "as he conspired [to do]," for a single witness who is rendered a zomem is exempt [from paying], and [as for] his own mouth regarding an admission, all the more so, since hazamah does not apply at all.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:9:2.hebrew: תאמר בעדים - אם הוזמו בחמשים שהעידו, משלמין ממון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4a:9:2.english: Would you say [the same] regarding witnesses - If they were rendered conspiring witnesses regarding the fifty [zuz] about which they testified, they pay money.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:12:1.hebrew: ותנא תונא אאידך דר' חייא - אנן סהדי דמאי דתפיס האי כו', פרש"י: כיון דהוי כהעדאת עדים, משתבע מדרבי חייא קמייתא. וקשה: כיון דלא מצי לאוכוחי הך ברייתא דהילך אלא מכח קמייתא, לימא ותנא תונא אקמייתא! לכך י"ל, דאנן סהדי לאו דוקא, דמאי דתפיס מחשבינן ליה השתא טפי מהעדאת עדים, וחשיב כאילו מודה ליה דדידיה הוא. אך קשה: דמ"מ איכא למיפרך דמתני', כי היכי דהאי מודה להאי האי נמי מודה להאי, ואפ"ה קמשתבעי, כדפריך אקמייתא; ומאי תיקן? וי"ל, דהשתא נמי מוכח מכח טעמא דבסמוך: אי הילך פטור, לא הוי מתקני רבנן שבועה דליכא דכוותה באורייתא; אבל לרבי חייא קמייתא, כי נמי בהעדאת עדים פטור, מתקני רבנן שבועה במתני', דחשיב הודאה במאי דתפיס חבריה. ודוחק, דלפ"ז הא דלא קאמר ותנא תונא אקמייתא משום דמאי דתפיס חשיב כהודאה, וזו לא היתה פירכתו למעלה, אלא מטעם כי היכי דאנן סהדי להאי כו':
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:12:1.english: "And the Tanna also taught" [was stated] with regard to another [statement] of Rabbi Ḥiyya - [Regarding the clause] "We are witnesses that what this one grasps, etc.," Rashi explained: Since it is equivalent to the testimony of witnesses, he takes an oath by virtue of the first [statement] of Rabbi Ḥiyya. And this is difficult: Since one cannot prove this baraita of heylakh [one who says: "Here you are"] except by virtue of the first [statement of Rabbi Ḥiyya], let [the Gemara] say: "And the Tanna taught [a support] for the first [statement]"! Therefore, one can say that "we are witnesses" is not meant literally; rather, what each one grasps we now consider to be more than the testimony of witnesses, and it is considered as though he admits to him that it is his. However, this is difficult: For nevertheless, one can [still] raise the objection against our mishna: Just as this one admits to that one, that one also admits to this one, and even so they take an oath — just as [the Gemara] objected against the first [statement]! What, then, did [this explanation] resolve? And one can say that now too, [the proof for heylakh] is derived by virtue of the reasoning stated nearby: If [one who says] heylakh is exempt [by Torah law], the Rabbis would not have instituted an oath that has no counterpart in the Torah. But according to the first [statement of] Rabbi Ḥiyya, even if one is exempt in the case of testimony of witnesses [by Torah law], the Rabbis could [still] institute an oath in our mishna, because [grasping] is considered an admission regarding what his fellow grasps. Yet this is strained, because according to this, the reason [the Gemara] did not say "And the Tanna taught [a support] for the first [statement]" would be because what [each one] grasps is considered like an admission, and this was not [the Gemara's] objection above; rather, [the objection was only] on the grounds that "just as we are witnesses for this one, etc."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:16:1.hebrew: ורב ששת אמר הילך פטור - נראה שהלכה כרב ששת, דבפ' השואל (לקמן בבא מציעא דף ק.) גבי עבד קטן פריך: ועוד הילך הוא. אך בספר חפץ משמע דהילך חייב [וע' תוס' ב"ב קכח: ד"ה הלכתא]:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:16:1.english: And Rav Sheshet says: "Here you are" is exempt - It appears that the halakha is in accordance with Rav Sheshet, for in chapter HaSho'el (below, Bava Metzia 100a), regarding a small slave, [the Gemara] objects: "And furthermore, it is [a case of] 'here you are'!" However, in Sefer Chefetz it implies that [one who says] "here you are" is obligated [to take an oath] [and see Tosafot, Bava Batra 128b, s.v. Hilkhata].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:4:1.hebrew: עד אחד יוכיח שישנו בהכחשה ובהזמה - שפיר גרס הכא ובהזמה, כיון שע"י הזמה דבורו בטל. ואין להקשות: מה לפיו שכן אינו משלם בהזמה, תאמר בעדים שמשלמין בהזמה, ואז לא יכול לומר עד אחד יוכיח שמשלם — כי מה שהעד אינו משלם כשהוא מוזם אינו חומרא, אלא לפי שבעדותו אינו מחייבו ממון; לכך, הואיל ודיבורו בטל, חשיב ישנו בהזמה. ובסמוך, על מה הצד פרכינן ליה, משום דעל מה הצד פרכינן פירכא כל דהו. ורבי חייא, אפי' על מה הצד לא פריך ליה, משום דמה שאינו משלם העד כשמוזם זהו גריעותו, לפי שלא היה כח בעדותו לחייב ממון:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:4:1.english: A single witness can prove [it], for he is subject to contradiction and to hazamah - It is a correct textual reading here [to include] "and to hazamah," since through hazamah his testimony is voided. And one should not object: "What [is notable] about [the admission of] his mouth? In that he does not pay through hazamah; would you say [the same] of [two] witnesses, who pay through hazamah?" — for then [the Gemara] would not be able to say "a single witness can prove [it]," [for does a single witness] pay?! For the fact that the [single] witness does not pay when he is rendered a zomem is not a stringency [of two witnesses over him], but rather [is merely] because by his testimony he does not obligate him in money; therefore, since his testimony is voided, he is considered "subject to hazamah." And nearby [on 4a:9], against the "common denominator," we do raise this refutation, because against a "common denominator" one may raise even a minimal refutation. And Rabbi Ḥiyya does not raise this refutation even against the "common denominator," because the fact that the [single] witness does not pay when he is rendered a zomem is his deficiency, since there was no power in his testimony to obligate money.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:6:1.hebrew: הצד השוה [שבהן] שע"י טענה כו' - וא"ת: כופר הכל יוכיח, שע"י טענה וכפירה פטור? ויש לומר, דבהצד השוה שבהן יש טענה חשובה, דכשמודה מקצת או עד מכחישו נראה דמשקר, ולכך יש שבועה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4a:6:1.english: The common denominator [between them] that through a claim, etc. - And if you say: Let [the case of one who] denies everything [kofer hakol] prove [otherwise], for through a claim and denial [it comes, and yet he is] exempt? And one can say that in the common denominator between them, there is a substantial claim, for when [the defendant] admits to part [of the claim] or a witness contradicts him, it appears that he is lying, and therefore there is an oath.
